title: Aexeo
summary: One platform for the customer side and the delivery side of the business: companies, licences, renewals, projects, learning and team schedules.
details: On the customer side, Aexeo keeps the company list with its branches and licences, MSA renewals, pricing, the plugin masterlist and proposals, with a proposal builder and templates. On the delivery side there are projects in waterfall or agile (phases, milestones, tasks, mandays, QA and problem-and-solution tracking), a Teams area with the schedule, leave, weekend support and a daily email digest, and a weekly dashboard. Around that sit a learning center with courses and assessments, SimForge for building interactive simulations, a mailer with an email builder, analytics, patch notes and Aria, an in-app assistant. Roles and permissions come from the database, so a new role needs no code change. The frontend is Next.js on a Laravel backend.

title: CMS backup and migration tool
summary: A small desktop tool that backs up, restores and seeds a CMS database without anyone touching the command line.
details: Setting up a new menu used to mean hand-editing migration files, dumping the database and hoping the images came along. I wrapped all of that in one window: back up the content and images into a single zip, restore it on another server, turn a menu dataset into a migration, and see what is still pending before anything runs. Anything that wipes data asks for a backup first and makes you type the database name. It builds into one portable exe, so it just gets copied to whichever machine needs it.

title: Store operations dashboard
summary: A dashboard that gives store managers one place to see stock, orders and daily sales, instead of juggling spreadsheets.
details: The team was copying numbers between spreadsheets every morning and things slipped through. I built the whole thing with them: talked through how their day actually runs, then made something quick to read and hard to get wrong. It now replaces the morning spreadsheet routine.

title: Order and request tracker
summary: An internal tool for logging requests, assigning them and seeing what is still waiting, so nothing gets lost in chat threads.
details: Requests used to live in messages and memory. This gives everyone a shared list with clear owners and statuses. I kept it deliberately simple so people would actually use it.

title: Desktop helper for the shop floor
summary: A small desktop app that handles a repetitive daily task for staff in a couple of clicks.
details: Some jobs just need to be fast and work offline. I built this for the people who do the same task all day, and it saves them real time every shift.
